goldens.comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully

The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `appStore` entries from module objects to `import(...)` promises (`packages/app-store/index.ts`). This forces all consumers to `await appStore[key]` (as many were updated). If any remaining/other consumer still does `const app = appStore[key]; if (app && "lib" in app ...)` without awaiting, the guard would evaluate false on a Promise and return `null`/`false` ("not implemented") rather than failing loudly. The diff doesn’t prove an unmigrated consumer still exists, but the change clearly creates this failure mode for any missed call site.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getVideoAdapters now throws on module-load failure instead of skipping gracefully, rejecting whole adapter list / deletes for callers like getBusyVideoTimes and deleteMeeting (videoClient.ts:21-34)

adjudication.rationale: In `videoClient.ts`, `getVideoAdapters` now does `const app = await appStore[appName as keyof typeof appStore];` where each `appStore[...]` entry is a dynamic `import(...)` Promise (per `packages/app-store/index.ts`). If any of those imports rejects (missing module, load error), the `await` will throw and abort the whole adapter-building loop; there is no try/catch to skip that credential. Callers like `getBusyVideoTimes` and `deleteMeeting` rely on `getVideoAdapters` and will fail rather than returning an empty/partial list, whereas previously indexing into `appStore` would not throw and would just skip when the adapter wasn't present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2 — Eager import() calls in packages/app-store/index.ts:5-35 are evaluated at module-load time, defeating lazy loading entirely; all app bundles load on every process start and consumers pay an extra await per lookup; should be () => import() thunks with Promise.all for multi-credential lookups

adjudication.rationale: In packages/app-store/index.ts the appStore object now initializes each entry with an immediate dynamic import expression (e.g., `applecalendar: import("./applecalendar")`, `caldavcalendar: import("./caldavcalendar")`, etc.). These `import()` calls are evaluated when the module is loaded, so all those Promise-based imports are kicked off at startup rather than on-demand. Consumers then do `await appStore[appName]` (e.g., in getCalendar.ts and videoClient.ts), which adds an await per lookup but does not restore true lazy loading. A thunk form like `() => import(...)` would defer loading until accessed, and multi-credential paths could then coordinate with Promise.all if desired.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1 — Fire-and-forget forEach(async ...) at packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts:125, packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts:125, and packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:553 swallows errors: returned promises are discarded so the surrounding try/catch no longer catches getCalendar/deleteEvent failures, causing unhandled rejections and silently skipped calendar/video cleanup; should use Promise.allSettled(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...)) inside the try

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes synchronous `forEach` callbacks into `forEach(async ...)` in `packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts`, `packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts`, and `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx`. In all three places the `forEach` is inside a `try { ... } catch { ... }`, but `Array.prototype.forEach` does not await returned promises, so exceptions/rejections from `await getCalendar(...)` or from `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` will not be caught by the surrounding try/catch and the returned promises are discarded. This can lead to unhandled promise rejections and skipped cleanup work, matching the finding’s claim; a `for..of` with `await` or `Promise.all/Promise.allSettled` over `map` would be needed to preserve error handling/awaiting semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2 — getCalendarCredentials in packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:28-31 now embeds unresolved Promises in credential tuples because getCalendar became async but is still called synchronously in .map(); other consumers may treat Promise as truthy calendar, making the falsy if (!calendar) guard unreachable and masking broken apps as 'connected'

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/CalendarManager.ts`, `getCalendarCredentials` still does `const calendar = getCalendar(credential);` even though `getCalendar` is now `async` (returns `Promise<Calendar | null>`). That means the returned tuple embeds a Promise in the `calendar` field unless every consumer explicitly awaits it. This PR updated `getConnectedCalendars` to `const calendar = await item.calendar;`, suggesting awareness, but the exported helper’s contract/type expectations and any other callers are not shown in the diff, so the claimed downstream masking/"guard unreachable" behavior cannot be verified here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3 — Serialized dynamic imports in cancel-path loop at packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:477-480: for...of with await getCalendar(credential) serializes adapter construction across credentials; Promise.all over filtered credentials would restore parallelism

adjudication.rationale: In handleCancelBooking.ts the diff replaces a synchronous getCalendar call with an async one and refactors the legacy branch from `.forEach(...)` to a `for (const credential of calendarCredentials) { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... }`. This does serialize `getCalendar` (and thus the underlying dynamic `import()` via `appStore[...]`) across credentials, whereas a `Promise.all(calendarCredentials.map(getCalendar))` pattern would allow parallel adapter/module loading. This is a performance/latency regression concern in the cancel/delete path, but not a correctness defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3 — Repeated await appStore[...] per credential in hot booking path (packages/core/videoClient.ts:21-35, packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:888): per-call awaits on the same module promise add overhead in the new-booking flow; if the eager-import map is fixed to thunks, these awaits introduce real chunk-load latency without the parallelism fix

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce `await appStore[...]` in `videoClient.ts`, but `appStore` now stores *already-created* `import("...")` promises (in `packages/app-store/index.ts`), so repeated awaits do not trigger repeated imports or add “chunk-load latency” the way thunks/on-demand imports would. Also, the cited `handleNewBooking.ts:888` change is `await getCalendar(credential)` (not an `await appStore[...]`), so the finding’s specific reference and latency claim are not grounded in what the diff shows and rely on a hypothetical future refactor (“fixed to thunks”).

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/CalendarManager.ts` `getCalendarCredentials` still does `const calendar = getCalendar(credential);` after `getCalendar` was changed to `async` (now `Promise<Calendar | null>`). That means the returned objects now contain a Promise in the `calendar` field. The diff shows one consumer (`getConnectedCalendars`) was updated to `await item.calendar`, but the API shape change is real and could trip any other consumers that still treat `calendar` as a `Calendar|null` value (a Promise is always truthy and has no `deleteEvent` etc.). The finding’s specific claim about “other consumers” throwing can’t be verified from this diff alone, but the underlying issue (Promise stored in return shape) is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Unawaited async callback in handleCancelBooking.ts:461 recurring-event deletion loop — calendar updates never awaited or collected, causing possible partial deletion of recurring events with a success response returned

adjudication.rationale: In handleCancelBooking.ts, the recurring-event branch uses `.forEach(async (credential) => { ... })` after changing `getCalendar` to async (`const calendar = await getCalendar(credential);`). `Array.forEach` does not await async callbacks, and the diff shows no collection/await of the resulting promises, so calendar update/delete operations inside that loop can run after the handler continues/returns, leading to partial recurring-event cleanup while still returning success.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: deleteEvent in packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:330 changed from sync function conditionally returning a Promise to an async function, changing contract semantics — previously sync failure paths returned undefined; now failures reject the returned Promise, risking unhandled rejections for callers that don't .catch()

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `deleteEvent` changed from a non-`async` function to `async`, but its declared return type was already `Promise<unknown>`. Previously, when `calendar` was falsy it returned `undefined` synchronously (despite the `Promise<unknown>` annotation); after the change it will resolve to `undefined` (i.e., `Promise.resolve(undefined)`), not reject. The finding’s claim that “previously sync failure paths returned undefined; now failures reject” is not supported by the shown code—no new rejection is introduced on the null-calendar path, and `calendar.deleteEvent(...)` could already reject before.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: getCalendarCredentials returns a now-async calendar without awaiting; depends on sole caller handling it, and other consumers may receive a Promise where they previously got a Calendar, silently breaking guards like if (!calendar) (CalendarManager.ts:28)

adjudication.rationale: In `CalendarManager.ts` `getCalendarCredentials` still does `const calendar = getCalendar(credential);` without `await` (and the function itself is not `async`), while `getCalendar` is now `async` and returns `Promise<Calendar|null>`. This means `calendar` in the returned objects is a Promise, and any consumer that doesn’t explicitly `await` it could mis-handle truthiness checks (a Promise is always truthy). The only shown consumer (`getConnectedCalendars`) was updated to `const calendar = await item.calendar;`, so the diff doesn’t prove a runtime bug here, but it does introduce a footgun/API change risk for other callers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Dynamic-import map in app-store/index.ts creates all import promises eagerly at module load, negating lazy-loading benefit, and a single failing chunk produces an unhandled rejection at startup

adjudication.rationale: In packages/app-store/index.ts, appStore is now initialized with values like `applecalendar: import("./applecalendar")`, which executes all dynamic imports immediately when the module is loaded, creating Promises for every entry up front (eagerly). This undermines lazy-loading (all chunks start loading at startup), and because many of these Promises may never be awaited (only the selected adapter is awaited elsewhere), any rejected import Promise can surface as an unhandled rejection originating at module initialization time.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Dynamic import failures now surface as request-time exceptions with no error handling in getCalendar, getVideoAdapters, and payment lookup call sites; a failed chunk load can fail an entire booking or cancel operation instead of degrading to 'app unavailable' (getCalendar.ts:14, videoClient.ts:23, handlePayment.ts:26, deletePayment.ts:16, handleCancelBooking.ts:589)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `appStore` entries from static module objects to `import("./...")` promises (packages/app-store/index.ts), and call sites now `await appStore[...]` (e.g., getCalendar.ts, videoClient.ts, handlePayment.ts, deletePayment.ts, handleCancelBooking.ts). None of these `await import()` paths are wrapped in `try/catch`, so a rejected dynamic import (e.g., chunk load failure) will throw and abort the request before the existing "not implemented"/"return null/false" fallback checks run. This is a concrete new failure mode introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: handleCancelBooking.ts:589 payment lookup — dirName keys may not match the camelCased appStore keys, and await undefined masks it silently; the as keyof typeof appStore cast suppresses compile-time checking so the payment flow silently no-ops on key mismatch

adjudication.rationale: The diff only changes payment lookups to `await appStore[...]` after `appStore` was converted to dynamic `import()` promises. The potential `dirName`/key mismatch and the `as keyof typeof appStore` cast already existed; the diff does not show any evidence that `dirName` values differ from the appStore keys. Also, a mismatch is not “silent”: the code explicitly checks `PaymentService` and `console.warn(...)` then returns `null`/`false` when `paymentApp` is missing/invalid. `await undefined` simply yields `undefined`, same end result as before.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Rejection handling removed from reschedule deletion path in bookings.tsx:553 — deleteEvent/deleteMeeting promises are completely orphaned, and the tRPC request can return success to the client while calendar cleanup failed (overlaps with issue 1)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx` the reschedule cleanup loop was changed to `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); ... })`. `Array.forEach` does not await async callbacks, so any returned `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` promises are not awaited/handled by the surrounding tRPC procedure. This can let the request complete successfully while calendar/video cleanup is still pending or fails (rejections can become unhandled).

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: forEach(async ...) in reschedule.ts, bookings.tsx, handleCancelBooking.ts discards the returned promise, making awaited deletion fire-and-forget — surrounding try blocks no longer catch errors and callers never await completion

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `forEach(async ...)` in multiple places (e.g. `packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts`, `packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts`, `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx`, and `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts`), where the body now `await`s `getCalendar(...)`. Since `Array.prototype.forEach` does not await returned promises, these deletions/updates become effectively fire-and-forget: the surrounding `try { ... } catch { ... }` cannot catch async rejections, and the caller will not wait for completion. This behavior change is directly caused by `getCalendar` becoming async and being awaited inside a `forEach` callback without collecting/awaiting the resulting promises.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: appStore[key] changed from module namespace to Promise; un-updated call sites without await receive a Promise, so 'lib' in promise is false and flows silently degrade to 'not implemented' returning null/false

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `appStore[key]` entries to dynamic `import()` Promises, but the shown call sites that perform `'lib' in app` / service checks are updated to `await` the Promise (e.g., `getCalendar.ts`, `videoClient.ts`, payment lookups in `handleCancelBooking.ts`, `deletePayment.ts`, `handlePayment.ts`, and `bookings.tsx`). No un-updated call site in this diff is verifiably doing `if (app && 'lib' in app ...)` on an un-awaited Promise, so the described silent degradation cannot be confirmed from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: getVideoAdapters now awaits dynamic imports sequentially per credential via for...of, delaying availability checks on cold starts with many video credentials

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/videoClient.ts`, `getVideoAdapters` was changed to an `async` function that iterates credentials with `for (const cred of withCredentials)` and does `const app = await appStore[appName as keyof typeof appStore];` inside the loop. Since `packages/app-store/index.ts` now sets each entry to a dynamic `import(...)` (a Promise), this makes module loading occur sequentially per credential, rather than concurrently (e.g., via `Promise.all`). That can increase cold-start latency when many video credentials are present, but it’s a performance/architecture concern rather than a correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Unhandled rejection risk from detached async forEach callbacks (e.g. failing calendar.deleteEvent) can crash the Node API server (Node ≥15 default behavior)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces multiple `array.forEach(async (...) => { ... await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) })` patterns (e.g. `packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts`, `packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts`, `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx`). Because `forEach` does not await returned promises, any rejection from `getCalendar(...)` or `calendar.deleteEvent(...)` will be detached from the surrounding control flow (including the nearby `try { ... } catch { ... }` blocks), creating an unhandled rejection risk and potentially leaving deletions incomplete/uncaught.
